alveolar macrophage and epithelial cells are the first line of defence against mycobacterial infection.

alveolar cells may play a crucial role in the innate immune defense against M. tuberculosis.
alveolar cells are not passive bystanders in the host response to tuberculosis but are actively involved in the innate immune defense against M. tuberculosis.
